skill.name: opencl-runtime
skill.description: Cross-vendor OpenCL runtime management and kernel development. Query platforms/devices, generate portable OpenCL C kernel code, handle vendor-specific extensions, manage contexts and command queues, compile and cache programs.

generated_query: I'm working on a real-time image processing pipeline that needs to run on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs using OpenCL. I have a 4000×3000 image and I need to apply a 7×7 Gaussian blur. I need help writing a portable OpenCL kernel that handles image borders correctly, uses local memory to reduce global memory accesses, and runs efficiently on both vendors. I also need the C host code to enumerate platforms and devices, create contexts and command queues (with profiling enabled), compile the kernel with appropriate build options (e.g., `-cl-fast-relaxed-math`), and cache the compiled binary to avoid recompilation. Finally, I need guidance on choosing the optimal local work-group size for each device based on its reported properties. Can you provide the full kernel source, the host code, and instructions for integrating this into my pipeline?

edit_instructions.rationale: The user explicitly asks for caching the compiled binary to avoid recompilation; deleting this step makes the skill unable to meet that requirement, while remaining otherwise complete.
Removes the local memory usage example and replaces it with a trivial global memory kernel, so the skill cannot demonstrate the local memory pattern required for the Gaussian blur kernel.
